correctness.rationale: The definition uses strict alternating lexicographic rotation minimality and forces primitive words. The elementary even-border parity contradiction compares two rotations after an even shared border. If an even-length Galois word has odd period d<=n/2, two rotations starting at kd and (k-1)d (n=kd+r) produce the same first differing letters at positions r+j and d+r+j of opposite parity, contradiction; proper powers excluded. Therefore any proper border b is odd and even n forces 2b<n. Odd n witnesses (01)^((n-1)/2)0 have every odd proper border; even n b=1 uses 010^(n-2) and b>=3 uses 010^(d-1)10^(b-2) with d=n-b, and strict rotation comparisons prove all witnesses Galois. Independently exhaustively enumerated all binary words n=2..13 and directly tested explicit witnesses for all allowed n<=69; both match. The infinite proof rests on the two-rotation obstruction and generic witnesses, not finite enumeration.

value.rationale: A natural combinatorial structural invariant of alternating-order Lyndon/Galois words: closes the gap from known border parity to the exact all-length existence spectrum, including a sharp new forbidden half-length region for even n and binary witnesses for every allowed odd b. It supplies a complete infinite-parameter classification valid for all ordered alphabets of size >=2, not an arbitrary finite slice or solely a restatement of old parity.

limitations: Existence of each proper border, not simultaneous border-set spectrum or number of words.
The all-n theorem follows the two-rotation proof; finite checks only through n=13 and witnesses through n=69 independently.
Possible unindexed stronger Galois period theory remains a best-of-knowledge priority risk.
